name: Prometheus/Grafana
description: Protects against destructive Prometheus/Grafana operations like deleting time series \ data or dashboards/datasources.

destructive_patterns.name: prometheus-rules-file-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Deleting Prometheus rule/config files can break alerting and monitoring coverage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Prometheus configuration or rule files stops alerting for the defined \ conditions. After Prometheus reloads, those alerts will no longer fire, \ potentially leaving critical conditions unmonitored.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - promtool check rules: Validate rule files before changes \ - Back up files before deletion \ - Use version control (git) for rule files

destructive_patterns.name: prometheus-tsdb-delete-series
destructive_patterns.description: Prometheus TSDB delete_series permanently deletes time series data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The delete_series admin endpoint permanently removes time series data matching \ the specified selectors. This data cannot be recovered. Historical metrics \ for the deleted series will show gaps.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Query the series first to verify what will be deleted \ - Use retention policies instead of manual deletion \ - Take a TSDB snapshot before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: kubectl-delete-prometheus-operator-resources
destructive_patterns.description: kubectl delete of Prometheus Operator resources (PrometheusRule/ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor) removes alerting/target configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Prometheus Operator CRDs removes alerting rules or scrape targets. \ The Prometheus Operator will update Prometheus configuration, potentially \ leaving services unmonitored.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kubectl get to review the resource first \ - kubectl describe to see what it configures \ - Export YAML before deletion: kubectl get -o yaml

destructive_patterns.name: grafana-cli-plugins-uninstall
destructive_patterns.description: grafana-cli plugins uninstall removes a Grafana plugin, potentially breaking dashboards.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Uninstalling a Grafana plugin breaks all dashboards using that plugin's panels \ or datasources. Users will see error messages where those panels were.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - grafana-cli plugins list: Review installed plugins first \ - Check which dashboards use the plugin before removal \ - Update the plugin instead of uninstalling

destructive_patterns.name: grafana-api-delete-dashboard
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Grafana dashboard removes all panels, queries, and configuration. \ Teams relying on this dashboard for monitoring will lose visibility.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /api/dashboards/uid/<uid> to export JSON first \ - Use Grafana provisioning for version-controlled dashboards \ - Use dashboard versioning in Grafana to restore later

destructive_patterns.name: grafana-api-delete-datasource
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a datasource breaks all dashboards and alerts using it. Panels will \ show 'Data source not found' errors, and alerting queries will fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the datasource first to verify the ID \ - Check which dashboards use this datasource \ - Use Grafana provisioning for datasource-as-code

destructive_patterns.name: grafana-api-delete-alert-notification
destructive_patterns.description: Grafana API DELETE /api/alert-notifications/... deletes alert notification channels.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a notification channel stops alert delivery to that destination. \ Alerts using this channel will fire but notifications won't be sent.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the notification channel first to verify the ID \ - Check which alerts use this notification channel \ - Disable the channel instead of deleting
